I made a block diagram for the PCB. The software was unusual and I am sure I made a lot of not optimal arrows, due to this I had to improvise a lot and stack arrows on each other or make a stray arrow of the right shape and adjust its length and generally most of the time went on checking if the connections made sense/ trying to wire everything. The question marks are requirements of each part which I looked up in the respected documentations which took a bit of time especially the esp32-s3 wroom-1.

This session was full of ups and downs. I decided to make a BoM and generally a "map" to follow as if I was solving a physics problem. Well as it turned out map maybe was as hard as the problem or maybe harder idk we will see. My main issues were how much time it took to get my thoughts together and map everything out in your brain first before the spreadsheet. Due to that countless spreadsheets variants had to be scratched and I eventually gave up on originality and just mirrored the steps of the professionals. The hard part number 2 was reassurance. Nobody was there to tell me if I understood everything right. Yes I llms served as a counterpart but it was often the case that I caught their mistakes and not the other way around. But the part that took the longest was finding the exact parts with their respective restrictions. JLCPCBs stock seemed to be completely drained of few components so improvisation had a place here and there.   Some parts like the pin budget were a much needed relief which felt both relaxing and rewarding.

Another day another shift. This one was the best by far. Barely any spreadsheets or typing. I finally got to the real PCB part but it came with nuances. First of all the software was of course a tiny bit quirky at the beginning but to be honest I adapted to it towards the end which made the process even more enjoyable. Of course it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows after all I've spent most of the time figuring out what's wrong and trying not to give up on as it would later turn out on the easiest things possible such as the whole capacitor charade which I thought would be incredibly difficult to understand but it turned out to be nothing more than fear mongering. But, we have a loss... I had to get rid of the camera since its footprint was mirrored and the often problems with ribbons plus high price and low use in resulted in it getting unfortunately eliminated.
